name: Challenge ProMode Arena (CPM physics)

scale.why: Quake III hull, 56 u tall, scaled to 1.8 m: 0.03214 m/u

gravity.source: https://github.com/id-Software/Quake-III-Arena/blob/master/code/game/g_main.c#L143 (Quake III's g_gravity 800; CPMA keeps the engine default)

ground_accel.note: as transcribed from CPM's developer docs by Xonotic's CPMA physics port

air_accel.note: CPM air with only a strafe key held (the bunny-hop strafe): accel 70 toward 30 u/s. With forward held too it is VQ3's accel 1 toward 320 u/s. Same formula as Quark's (accel x min(wish, cap)); Quark multiplies air_accel by 10, so 70 -> 7.

air_cap.note: the wish speed the air push aims at

jumpHeight.note: v^2/2g, before CPM's double jump; Quark: 1.22 m

timeTo90.source: derived from this file's speed, ground_accel, friction, stop_speed
timeTo90.note: Quake ground model at 1 ms steps (friction then accelerate), the same way Quark's physsim measures its own run_up / stop presets; Quark: 0.072 s

stopDistance.source: derived from this file's speed, friction, stop_speed
stopDistance.note: Quake ground model at 1 ms steps (friction then accelerate), the same way Quark's physsim measures its own run_up / stop presets; Quark: 1.21 m

stopTime.source: derived from this file's speed, friction, stop_speed
stopTime.note: Quake ground model at 1 ms steps (friction then accelerate), the same way Quark's physsim measures its own run_up / stop presets; Quark: 0.364 s

extras: air control 150 with W only (sv_aircontrol 150, 'from cpm1_dev_docs'): Quark's air_control is modelled on it but is a different formula (Quark 4, 'rad/s-ish')
air stop acceleration 2.5 when pushing against your velocity (sv_airstopaccelerate 2.5): Quark softens this instead (overstrafe)
double jump and ramp jumps (a jump soon after landing goes higher; numbers not sourced here)
notes: Numbers from Xonotic's physicsCPMA.cfg, which cites the CPM developer docs line by line; CPMA's own source isn't public. Quark's air model (CPM-style W-only air control plus A/D strafing toward a small cap) is closest to this family.
